speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; how old are you and exactly how long has this swelling been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (specifically Oligoarticular JIA).

Given the patient's age (18 months), the presence of monoarticular swelling in the right knee without trauma, and the family history suggesting an autoimmune predisposition, the clinical picture strongly points to Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis. I am requesting inflammatory markers and a blood count to confirm the diagnosis and rule out infection.

REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, CBC. REQUEST IMAGES: Right Knee X-Ray.
